    Top-level proof of SHA-3 security, with failing oracles (EasyCrypt proof/SHA3OSecurity.ec) — #

    EC-fidelity port

    Ported so far: the clones SORO, SH, the file's modules (EC l. 1–175), and the local modules of section Preimage (EC l. 194–300) with its first lemmas, rw_RF_List_While (EC l. 301), eq_IRO_RFWhile (EC l. 337), eq_extend (EC l. 430), of_listK, Fill_In, eq_eager_ideal (EC l. 492), eq_eager_ideal2 (EC l. 512), Dist, Game, eager_ideal (EC l. 574), rw_ideal_2 (EC l. 652), rw_ideal (EC l. 792), leq_ideal (EC l. 870), rw_real (EC l. 881) and Sponge_preimage_resistant (EC l. 898): section Preimage is complete. Section SecondPreimage is complete too: its local modules Dist_of_P2Adv, SORO_P2, Dist, Game, eager_ideal (EC l. 1298), toto (EC l. 1427), titi (EC l. 1442), rw_ideal_2 (EC l. 1476), rw_ideal (EC l. 1638), leq_ideal (EC l. 1727), rw_real (EC l. 1738), TOTO and Sponge_second_preimage_resistant (EC l. 1781). Section Collision (EC l. 1808–2651) is complete: Dist_of_CollAdv, SORO_Coll, Dist, Game, eager_ideal, rw_ideal_2, rw_ideal, leq_ideal, rw_real and Sponge_collision_resistant. The file is ported in full.

    Translation:

    • the file-level type f_out, the operators size_out, sigma, dout, to_list, of_list and their axioms are the first port's class SHA3OSecurity.Params; doutE1 is the first port's;
    • clone import SecureORO as SORO with …, clone import SecureHash as SH with … are clone over the pilot theories (Syntax/Clone.lean), their realizes the clones' proof *. Both are imported, as in EC; where a name is in both (Bounder, Preimage, AdvPreimage, …) it is written with its clone (SH.AdvPreimage), as EC does where it matters;
    • EC's import OIndif (the clone of SHA3_OIndiff): the sponge's module types (OFUNCTIONALITY, ODPRIMITIVE, …) are the first port's SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif; SH's own are SH.OIndif.…, as EC's OIndif.OFUNCTIONALITY after the clone;
    • FSetSize(F) aliases init: EC's alias (proc f = c;, since 2026-11-20); OSponge(P) = FSetSize(CSome(Sponge, P)) is Module.comp FSetSize (CSome Sponge).
    • EC's module types are structural: a sponge-level OFUNCTIONALITY is an ODFUNCTIONALITY, an OPRIMITIVE an ODPRIMITIVE of SH.OIndif too. Here each such use is a coercion, declared once (module_subtype);
    • EC's theory Program (the clone PBool: Sample, LoopSnoc, Sample_LoopSnoc_eq) is the first port's PBool.LoopSnoc.sample and the rule prhlStmt_dlist_left (Lib/EC/DListCall.lean); EC's two transitivity steps through Sample.sample and LoopSnoc.sample are one, its first leg the lemma Preimage.dlist_LoopSnoc (as in E12);
    • the sections' operators on maps (inv, eq_extend_size) and the value lemmas about them that EC proves inline by smt (inv_fresh, eq_extend_size_set_lt, …) are the first port's;
    • FSetSize's proc get = f (outside its module type) makes FSetSize(F) an Oracle in EC: a coercion of SH.OIndif.OFUNCTIONALITY to SORO.Oracle (get is f);
    • (GAP 1, closed 2026-11-23: a loop that does not write a variable the condition after it reads is EC's conseq (: _ ==> true) and while I, with EC's frame;)
    • clone import FullRO as Eager with … is the first port's namespace SHA3OSecurity.Eager (RO_T, RO, LRO, the variables Eager.RO.m, Eager.FRO.m), re-exported under Eager;
    • a variable of an inlined callee whose name is also one of the other side, or of the precondition at another type (x1{1}, x0{2}), and a variable the statement no longer mentions (k after wp, in splitwhile's condition) are written with their lenses, §(localVarLens "x0" (List Bool)){2} (GAP 2);
    • GAP 3 (closed): the first port's ODRestr hands the adversary its primitive built with the first port's module type constructor, which the clone SH's projections did not see through; proc and inline* open it since 2026-11-17 (procedures across clones' module types), and the hand simp only [ODPRIMITIVE_f_mk] lines left over from before went on 2026-11-21;
    • GAP 4 (closed 2026-11-21): after sp through a game's initializations, glob A is equal in the two memories by the memories' equation, which was taken out by hand; ec_progress reads it off now (mem_eq_read), and ec_auto reads glob A past other modules' writes;
    • GAP 5 (closed 2026-11-21): equiv_call (_ : ={x₁, …}) on the adversary put ={glob A} into the oracles' judgments (EC's do not have it), on which inline did not end; it now gives EC's oracle judgments, so the invariants are EC's single equality sets;
    • a call behind the module type's record ((SORO.RF_T.get RFList)) keeps the other variables only with its footprint stated at that spelling (fvP_RF_T_get_RFList, fvP_SORO_Bounder, fvP_RFWhile: EC reads them off the code);
    • EC's rnd f g between dlist dbool size_out and dout is equiv_rnd (fun l => oget (of_list l)): it asks that f push the first distribution to the second, which is the first port's dlist_dout (EC's dout_equal_dlist, to_listK);
    • GAP 8 (closed 2026-11-21): conseq (: _ ==> Q) in front of the adversary's call did not keep a variable neither the adversary nor its oracles write (Dist_of_P2Adv.m; EC's does); its frame now does (Stmt.Keeps.call_app_writes), and the call's invariant is EC's;
    • byequiv with a fact about &m where one game takes a parameter: the judgment is written out, byequiv (?last : equiv[ … ~ ….main (m1) : … ∧ §Dist_of_P2Adv.m{1} = mess ∧ §m1{2} = mess ==> (§res{1} → §res{2}) ]);
    • GAP 9: the parameter names of a clone's game (SH.SecondPreimage(A, …).main) and of a module with a Lean parameter (TOTO(A).main) are not known: EC's byphoare(: arg = mess ==> _) and call(: arg = mess /\ … ==> res) are byphoare (?j : phoare[ ….main (m) : … ] ≤ …) and phoare_call (?spec : phoare[ ….main (m1) : … ] ≤ …), the judgments written out with their bound (which also gives the relation the form phoare_call reads; plain byphoare's is a lambda);
    • GAP 10: sim / Dist_of_P2Adv.m (EC's sim between the game and TOTO, which sets Dist_of_P2Adv.m first) leaves the last implication, the reads through the calls' writes: one simp by hand;
    • GAP 11 (closed 2026-11-22): sp over Dist_of_P2Adv.m <- m stated its fact at a spelling the closers did not identify with the later read; EC's sp and auto go through now;
    • EC's bypr (pHL) is the new bypr (Logic/ByPr.lean); byphoare's bound is a real, whose 0 ≤ x is a side goal EC does not have;
    • Countable f_out (from to_list_inj) is the side condition of SORO.RO_is_second_preimage_resistant;
    • GAP 6: a game of the clone SH applied to the sponge's modules (SH.Preimage(A, OSponge, PSome(Perm))) has them behind the clone's projections and coercions, which inline does not open: OPRIMITIVE_coe_eq, OSponge_app, PSome_Perm_init (all by rfl) put them at the sponge's module types first;
    • GAP 7 (closed 2026-11-22): sim did not end on two loops that call the permutation after a conseq that keeps glob Perm: a call's result is now replaced in sim's equality set by the call's arguments and the callee's globals (EC's backward analysis), and what sim leaves of the precondition is closed by auto_close;
    • EC's chains inline{1} 1; inline{2} 1; sp down to the adversary's call are repeat stmt_inline{1} 0; repeat stmt_inline{2} 0; stmt_sp; sim n n in front of a call or a conditional is stmt_wp (sim n n where a sampling is left);
    • EC's alias{1} 1 mp = BIRO.IRO.mp names the map before a loop: equiv_exists* §IRO.mp{1};
    • in section Collision, an inlined game's locals m1, m2 (hash1, hash2) are renamed m10, m20 (hash10, hash20) on the side whose other side has variables of those names: EC's ={m1, m2} is then §m10{1} = §m1{2} ∧ §m20{1} = §m2{2}; toto and titi of that section are textually SecondPreimage's, and are that section's;
    • the local modules and lemmas of sections SecondPreimage and Collision that do not mention the section's adversary (FInit … Fill_In; rw_RF_List_While, eq_IRO_RFWhile, eq_extend, of_listK, eq_eager_ideal, eq_eager_ideal2) are textually those of section Preimage in EC: they are Preimage's here, opened in the later sections;
    • where EC opens two queries after the adversary's call together and cases on the first one's counter test (so that sim n n applies), they are taken one after the other with seq, each by EC's steps for one query;
    • the sections' local modules are modules of the namespace of their section (Preimage.FInit, …); their variables (Log.m, RFList.m) are global_vars, which the section's adversary is restricted against (fresh in EC); a local module that takes the section's adversary has it as a Lean parameter (Dist_of_P1Adv A, SORO_P1 A).

    Declarations of the first port #

    Definitions and plain lemmas of the first port of this file (2026-10/11) that the proofs below use; its program-logic proofs are gone.

    The first port's translation notes (some mention declarations that went with its proofs):

    • The file-level abstract type f_out, operators size_out, dout, to_list, of_list and the axioms (including sigma_ge0, an axiom about the defined sigma) are the parameter class Params, as in SHA3Security.
    • Name resolution follows EasyCrypt's (checked with print): unqualified OFUNCTIONALITY … are SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif's; OIndif.X is SH.OIndif.X (the clone SH comes later); Oracle and RF are SORO's; RO, FRO, LRO are Eager's.
    • clone import SecureORO as SORO, clone import SecureHash as SH, clone import FullRO as Eager are namespaces of abbreviations that declare the clones' module variables; their realizes are SORO.axioms, SH.axioms.
    • FSetSize and ExtendOutput have proc get = f, a procedure outside their type: it is FSetSize.get, the same procedure as FSetSize.f (an abbreviation). Their aliases of a parameter's procedures are EC's (proc f = c;, since 2026-11-20), as are FInit's, PInit's, OF's, ExtendSample's and Fill_In's, and the sections' Dist's (whose distinguish takes EC's d_in_t = unit as (): PROM's RO_LRO_D takes any procedure signature). OSponge(P) = FSetSize(CSome(Sponge, P)) is Module.comp FSetSize (CSome Sponge); OFC2(F) = OFC(ExtendOutputSize(F)) is Module.comp OFC ExtendOutputSize, written out where it is called inside a module body.
    • The sections' local modules have variables (Log.m, RFList.m, Dist_of_P2Adv.m): lens parameters of the local declarations, with freshness hypotheses (LocalFresh, exception E6). Log has only its variable, so it is that lens alone. The sections' local declarations go into namespaces named after the sections.
    • OIndif(F, OSimulator(F), D) (from SHA3_OIndiff) is written IdealGame F D.

    Type 1

    EasyCrypt's file-level abstract type and operators, with their axioms: op size_out with size_out_gt0, axiom sigma_ge0, type f_out, op dout with dout_ll, dout_fu, dout_full, op to_list, op of_list with spec_dout, spec2_dout, to_list_inj, to_listK and dout_equal_dlist.

    • size_out : ℤ
    • size_out_gt0 : 0 < size_out
    • sigma_ge0 : 0 ≤ SHA3Indiff.limit
    • f_out : Type
    • f_out_inhabited : Inhabited f_out
    • dout : SubProbability f_out
    • dout_ll : EC.is_lossless dout
    • dout_fu : EC.is_funiform dout
    • dout_full : EC.is_full dout
    • to_list : f_out → List Bool
    • of_list : List Bool → Option f_out
    • spec_dout (l : f_out) : EC.size (to_list l) = size_out
    • spec2_dout (l : List Bool) : EC.size l = size_out → of_list l ≠ none
    • to_list_inj : Function.Injective to_list
    • to_listK (e : f_out) (l : List Bool) : to_list e = l ↔ of_list l = some e
    • dout_equal_dlist : (do let x ← dout pure (to_list x)) = EC.dlist EC.dbool size_out

                                                                                                                                                                                        A sponge-level primitive used as a DPRIMITIVE of the clone SH (in SH.Preimage, for OSponge) is the same module used as the sponge's (EC's module types are structural): the two coercions build it with the two module types' projections.

                                                                                                                                                                                          noncomputable def GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.SecondPreimage.Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvSecondPreimage) :
                                                                                                                                                                                          Module.Arr SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODFUNCTIONALITY (Module.Arr SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODPRIMITIVE (procmod () → Bool))

                                                                                                                                                                                          proc distinguish of module Dist_of_P2Adv as a module, abstracted over the module parameters it uses (F, P, in declaration order): Module.Arr … (Module.Proc (procsig …)).

                                                                                                                                                                                          Apply it with the @[simp] lemma Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.apply_simp, which fills the holes of Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure with the callees the body called.

                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                            noncomputable def GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.SecondPreimage.Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvSecondPreimage) :
                                                                                                                                                                                            proctype () → Bool uses ((List Bool) → List Bool, (List Bool) → Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out)

                                                                                                                                                                                            The body of proc distinguish of module Dist_of_P2Adv, as a procedure of its own: the 2 calls it makes to module parameters (F, P) are its holes, in the order the body makes them.

                                                                                                                                                                                            A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish for this procedure as a module.

                                                                                                                                                                                            Equations
                                                                                                                                                                                            • One or more equations did not get rendered due to their size.
                                                                                                                                                                                            Instances For
                                                                                                                                                                                              source
                                                                                                                                                                                              @[simp]
                                                                                                                                                                                              theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.SecondPreimage.Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvSecondPreimage) (F : SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODFUNCTIONALITY) (P : SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODPRIMITIVE) :
                                                                                                                                                                                              Module.app (Module.app (distinguish A) F) P = Module.proc ((procedure A).instantiate ((Module.app A (Module.pair (OptionIndifferentiability.ODFUNCTIONALITY.mk { f := DFSetSize(F).f }) P)).procedure, DFSetSize(F).f.procedure))

                                                                                                                                                                                              @[simp]: applying Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish to the parameters proc distinguish uses (F, P) is Module.proc (Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure.instantiate …) — the procedure with its holes filled by the callees they were made from, each written as it was in the body (with the arguments in place of the module parameters) and turned into a Procedure by Module.Proc.procedure.

                                                                                                                                                                                              source
                                                                                                                                                                                              @[simp]
                                                                                                                                                                                              theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.SecondPreimage.Dist_of_P2Adv.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvSecondPreimage) (F : SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODFUNCTIONALITY) (P : SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODPRIMITIVE) :
                                                                                                                                                                                              Dist_of_P2Adv(A, F, P).distinguish = Module.app (Module.app (distinguish A) F) P

                                                                                                                                                                                              @[simp]: applying Dist_of_P2Adv to a tuple of its 2 parameters F, P — the record of its procedures Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish, each applied to the parameters it uses.

                                                                                                                                                                                              This is the lemma that unfolds a module use: simp rewrites with it, then with the field lemmas of the module type (N.f.mk_simp) to get at the one procedure the goal is about, and then with Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.apply_simp to fill that procedure's holes.

                                                                                                                                                                                              source
                                                                                                                                                                                              theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.SecondPreimage.Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvSecondPreimage) (holeArgs✝ : (HoleSigs.cons (procsig (List Bool) → List Bool) (HoleSigs.cons (procsig (List Bool) → Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out) HoleSigs.empty)).Instantiation) :
                                                                                                                                                                                              (procedure A).instantiate holeArgs✝ = proc () : Bool { var m' : List Bool, hash : Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out, hash' : Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out; Preimage.Log.m <- EC.FMap.empty; m' <- call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero) (§m); hash <- call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero.succ) (§m); hash' <- call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero.succ) (§m'); return decide (§m ≠ §m' ∧ ∃ (y : SHA3OSecurity.f_out), §hash' = some y ∧ §hash = some y) }

                                                                                                                                                                                              Instantiating the holes of Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure with a tuple holeArgs of procedures: the body of proc distinguish as written, with each hole call replaced by the matching holeArgs.lookup (HoleIndex.zero being the first hole the body declared). True by rfl.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Deliberately not @[simp], unlike the other apply_simp lemmas: its right-hand side is the whole body written out, so letting it fire on its own would turn any goal mentioning an instantiated procedure into that body. Inlining a procedure is a step to ask for by name (simp [Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp]).

                                                                                                                                                                                              source
                                                                                                                                                                                              noncomputable def GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.SecondPreimage.Dist_of_P2Adv [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvSecondPreimage) :
                                                                                                                                                                                              Module.Arr (Module.Prod SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODFUNCTIONALITY SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODPRIMITIVE) (procmod () → Bool)

                                                                                                                                                                                              The module declared by module Dist_of_P2Adv, abstracted over its 2 parameters F, P, which it takes as one right-nested tuple: Module.Arr (T₁ ×ₘ (… ×ₘ Tₙ)) M, with M the anonymous product of the procedures' own types, the declaration naming no module type.

                                                                                                                                                                                              Applied to such a tuple it is the record of its procedures Dist_of_P2Adv.distinguish, each applied to the parameters that procedure itself uses — which is what the @[simp] lemma Dist_of_P2Adv.apply_simp says.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      noncomputable def GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.Collision.Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish.procedure [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvCollision) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                      proctype () → Bool uses (() → List Bool × List Bool, (List Bool) → Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The body of proc distinguish of module Dist_of_CollAdv, as a procedure of its own: the 2 calls it makes to module parameters (F, P) are its holes, in the order the body makes them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                      A hole stands for a call whose callee is not known here — a module parameter is supplied only when the module is applied — so the body is a ProcedureWithHoles, to be instantiated (see Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp) rather than run. Use Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish for this procedure as a module.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                        theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.Collision.Dist_of_CollAdv.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvCollision) (F : SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODFUNCTIONALITY) (P : SHA3_OIndiff.OIndif.ODPRIMITIVE) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Dist_of_CollAdv(A, F, P).distinguish = Module.app (Module.app (distinguish A) F) P

                                                                                                                                                                                                                        @[simp]: applying Dist_of_CollAdv to a tuple of its 2 parameters F, P — the record of its procedures Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish, each applied to the parameters it uses.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                        This is the lemma that unfolds a module use: simp rewrites with it, then with the field lemmas of the module type (N.f.mk_simp) to get at the one procedure the goal is about, and then with Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish.apply_simp to fill that procedure's holes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem GaudisCrypt.SHA3.Pilot.SHA3OSecurity.Collision.Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp [SLCommon.Params] [BlockSponge.Params] [Gconcl_list.Params] [SHA3OSecurity.Params] (A : SH.AdvCollision) (holeArgs✝ : (HoleSigs.cons (procsig () → List Bool × List Bool) (HoleSigs.cons (procsig (List Bool) → Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out) HoleSigs.empty)).Instantiation) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                            (procedure A).instantiate holeArgs✝ = proc () : Bool { var m1 : List Bool, m2 : List Bool, hash1 : Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out, hash2 : Option SHA3OSecurity.f_out; Preimage.Log.m <- EC.FMap.empty; m1, m2 <- call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero) (); hash1 <- call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero.succ) (§m1); hash2 <- call (holeArgs✝.lookup HoleIndex.zero.succ) (§m2); return decide (§m1 ≠ §m2 ∧ ∃ (y : SHA3OSecurity.f_out), §hash1 = some y ∧ §hash2 = some y) }

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Instantiating the holes of Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish.procedure with a tuple holeArgs of procedures: the body of proc distinguish as written, with each hole call replaced by the matching holeArgs.lookup (HoleIndex.zero being the first hole the body declared). True by rfl.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Deliberately not @[simp], unlike the other apply_simp lemmas: its right-hand side is the whole body written out, so letting it fire on its own would turn any goal mentioning an instantiated procedure into that body. Inlining a procedure is a step to ask for by name (simp [Dist_of_CollAdv.distinguish.procedure.apply_simp]).
